papers.tldr: Lean 4の証明をリファクタリングし、ソースの長さとチェックコストを削減する手法を提案し、QwenモデルとCodex CLIを活用して証明の置き換えを行った結果、全127の証明バージョンチェックに合格し、Lean Refactor ArenaのオープンソースLLMトラックで1位を獲得した。

papers.title: Xtream: An Explicit Metric State for Large-Scale Streaming Reconstruction
papers.summary: 3D foundation models (3DFMs) enable dense reconstruction in a feed-forward pass, yet their effective span is limited by cross-view attention. Local consistency has been expanded through geometric alignment of video chunks and recursive updates of an implicit memory, and large-scale scenes with pose graphs. However, both strategies are prone to drift, largely due to the lack of metric-scale observability from monocular geometry. We present Xtream,a hybrid streaming pipeline that maintains an explicit metric state through a factor graph over keyframes, while using a 3DFM as a geometric front end. Xtream incorporates metric information in two ways: through metric scale predictions from 3DFMs; or through inertial measurements if available. Across the large-scale benchmarks of VBR, Oxford Spires and KITTI, Xtream achieves state-of-the-art performance in 3DFM-based online reconstruction, reducing average absolute trajectory errors compared with published baselines and concurrent work. https://ernestolozano.github.io/xtream
papers.tldr: Xtreamは、3D基盤モデルを用いた大規模ストリーミング再構築のためのハイブリッドパイプラインで、キー フレーム上のファクターグラフを通じて明示的なメトリック状態を維持し、3DFMからのメトリックスケール予測や慣性測定を取り入れることで、最新の性能を達成しています。

papers.title: TACT-Bench: Testing Adaptive Conversational Threats against Tool-Use Agents
papers.summary: The growing autonomy of AI agents in using external tools and making decisions has created an urgent need for comprehensive safety benchmarks. Existing benchmarks test compromised tool channels or adaptive multi-turn attacks, though they may not capture the unique capabilities of policy-governed tool-use agents, which must resist unauthorized requests without abandoning the legitimate work embedded in the same interaction. To fill this gap, we introduce TACT-Bench, a stateful benchmark built around scenario-specific stories, personas, manipulation tactics, and response-adaptive escalation. Each adversarial task targets an action explicitly prohibited by the policy provided to the assistant, while the policy remains hidden from the attacking user. TACT pairs each adversarial task with at least one benign counterpart, and its adversarial tasks retain authorized ground-truth actions when a compliant resolution remains available. We define these base tasks as TACT-Base. We additionally introduce TACT-TrustPrime, which places an independent benign task before an unrelated attack in the same conversation. We also propose Paired Selective Trustworthiness (PST), which combines explicit safe refusal with demonstrated capability on matched benign tasks, to analyze an agent's overcautiousness and practicality. Averaged across 6 different models as assistants, TACT-Base raises Attack-Induced Failure Rate (AFR) by 17.53% over four compatible attack baselines, and TACT-TrustPrime raises it by a further 17.01%. The two evaluated defense methods reduce AFR by only 8.35%--9.41% on average and do not consistently improve PST, underscoring the need for stronger policy-enforcement methods.
papers.tldr: TACT-Benchは、ポリシーに基づくツール使用エージェントに対する適応型脅威をテストするための新しいベンチマークで、攻撃者がポリシーを隠した状態で禁止された行動を狙うタスクを提供します。このベンチマークは、エージェントの安全性を評価するために、攻撃誘発失敗率（AFR）を大幅に引き上げることが示されており、より強力なポリシー執行手法の必要性を強調しています。

papers.title: RVLM-X: Towards a Universal VLM Harness
papers.summary: Harnesses for vision-language models (VLMs) have grown with the models' capabilities, notably for images far larger than those seen in training, where downscaling loses small details. Most of them wrap the VLM in a fixed procedure, such as a zoom tree, that decides in advance where it looks and how the evidence is combined. These procedures make up for the weaknesses of older models by keeping them on a task-specific path, but with frontier models that reliably plan and use tools, they can lower accuracy. We propose RVLM-X, a task-generalizable recursive VLM harness that runs unchanged across photographs, charts and maps. Following the recursive inference of Recursive Language Models, the VLM programmatically controls its own visual context in a code REPL that holds the full-resolution image and calls itself recursively on regions that it chooses. With a cost-efficient frontier model as the base of every method, RVLM-X is more accurate than a single call on all 7 public benchmarks and has the highest pooled accuracy. Because existing benchmarks mostly test whether a model finds one small detail, we also introduce MapGenBench, procedurally generated maps whose questions combine fine-detail perception with multi-step reasoning. There, RVLM-X answers 71.4% of held-out questions against 55.5% for the strongest baseline. Overall, our findings suggest that as VLMs plan and use tools more reliably, letting the model write its own visual search works better than fixing one in advance.
papers.tldr: RVLM-Xは、視覚と言語のモデル（VLM）のための汎用的なハーネスで、プログラム的に自身の視覚コンテキストを制御し、全7つの公開ベンチマークで単一呼び出しよりも高い精度を示します。また、新たに導入されたMapGenBenchでは、71.4%の正答率を達成し、従来のモデルを上回る性能を発揮しています。

papers.title: FN-Prune: Training-Free Expert Pruning with Finite RMSNorm Perturbations
papers.summary: Expert pruning reduces the memory footprint of mixture-of-experts language models, but retaining model quality depends on which experts are removed. Frequency- and magnitude-based scores measure the expert in isolation and overlook how normalization consumes its contribution: subtracting one expert changes both the direction of the residual stream and the scale applied to what remains. We propose FN-Prune, a training-free criterion that compares the next RMSNorm outputs before and after subtracting each router-weighted expert contribution, holding original routes and weights fixed. Squared differences are averaged over all calibration tokens in one pass; low-scoring experts are physically deleted at uniform per-layer ratios, and inference reroutes among survivors. At 50% expert removal, FN-Prune achieves lower WikiText-2 perplexity than the best published methods on Qwen3, ERNIE, and OLMoE, including a 32% reduction on OLMoE. At the same budget, GSM8K accuracy improves over the best published methods by 7.5 and 7.0 percentage points on Qwen3 and ERNIE, respectively, while multiple-choice gains remain task-dependent.
papers.tldr: FN-Pruneは、トレーニングなしでミクスチャー・オブ・エキスパート言語モデルのエキスパートプルーニングを行う手法で、50%のエキスパート削除でWikiText-2のパープレキシティを改善し、GSM8Kの精度も向上させることに成功しました。

papers.title: LeanWAM: Learning Latent World Action Models from Frozen Video Models
papers.summary: World action models (WAMs) typically adapt large pretrained video generators to jointly predict future observations and robot actions, incurring substantial training and deployment costs. However, it remains unclear which future representations a policy actually needs and how compactly they can be represented. Our probing study shows that complementary future representations can be compressed into a few tokens while retaining most of their action-decoding performance. Motivated by this finding, we introduce LeanWAM, a latent WAM that transfers video priors from a frozen video generator to a lightweight policy via two-stage training. In the first stage, a Future Extractor compresses observed transitions into 32 predictive tokens. These tokens condition the frozen generator and are jointly shaped by action, RGB, semantic, and geometric supervision, while a compact readout of the generator's hidden states supplies complementary world tokens. The second stage distills both representations into the policy, which learns to predict them from current observations while generating actions. With 1.4B parameters and no large-scale embodied pretraining, LeanWAM outperforms strong vision-language-action (VLA) and WAM baselines on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboTwin~2.0. It predicts an action chunk in 25.1\,ms on an A100 GPU, 12.3--41.5$\times$ faster than representative WAMs. These results demonstrate that compact predictive supervision can transfer video priors to robust and efficient control.
papers.tldr: LeanWAMは、フローズンビデオモデルからの知識を活用し、未来の観測とロボットの行動を効率的に予測するための軽量なワールドアクションモデルです。この手法は、32の予測トークンを用いて高いパフォーマンスを維持しつつ、従来のモデルよりも大幅に高速なアクション予測を実現しています。
